_source: HCM 7th Edition, Chapter 29 (Urban Street Facilities: Supplemental), Section 5, Example Problem 1: Automobile-Oriented Urban Street, EASTBOUND direction (Exhibits 29-39 through 29-49). 1-mi downtown facility of five segments with signalized boundary intersections: Segments 1-3 are 1,320 ft at a 35 mi/h speed limit, Segments 4-5 are 660 ft at 30 mi/h; two through lanes per direction. Per-segment performance measures are the published Chapter 18 outputs supplied as inputs to the Chapter 16 aggregation (Exhibit 16-7 'HCM method output'): Segment 1 (Exhibit 29-47) base FFS 40.9 mi/h, travel speed 24.2 mi/h, spatial stop rate 1.72 stops/mi, LOS C; Segment 5 (Exhibit 29-48) base FFS 37.9 mi/h, travel speed 17.6 mi/h, stop rate 2.63 stops/mi, LOS D. Segments 2-3 are not individually published and assume Segment 1's values; Segment 4 assumes Segment 5's (the chapter states segment geometry/volumes are identical within each group; only signal offsets differ). Published facility results (Exhibit 29-49, eastbound): base free-flow speed 40.1 mi/h (EXACT, all segment base FFS values published), travel speed 22.6 mi/h and spatial stop rate 1.83 stops/mi (approximate here: 22.1 and 1.95, because the unpublished Segments 2-4 differ from the copied values), LOS C (exact), poorest-performing segment LOS D (exact). The v/c ratios (0.85/0.90) are representative undersaturated values consistent with the published LOS (the exhibit reports them only via the v/c<=1.0 criterion). The test drives UrbanFacility::aggregate() on these published segment measures.
